title: Microsoft 365 Backup: longer recovery windows for SharePoint and OneDrive, up to 10 years
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the recovery windows, unchanged one-year default, policy controls and consumption billing. The roadmap dates and later documentation dates are accurately distinguished, and the workload-specific administrator roles match the current setup page.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the ability to set longer retention periods to restore beyond one year.
claims.quote: This creates the ability to set longer term retention periods to restore beyond one year.

claims.claim: SharePoint policies support 3 months, 6 months, or any whole number of years from 1 through 10.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing one-year default is unchanged, and existing policies keep it unless an administrator changes them.
claims.quote: The existing one-year default is unchanged. ... Existing policies keep a one-year recovery window unless an administrator changes them.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Existing policies keep a one-year recovery window unless an administrator changes them.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The recovery window is set per backup policy.
claims.quote: You set the recovery window on a policy, and it applies to every artifact in that policy.

claims.claim: A policy's recovery window applies to every item in that policy.
claims.quote: You set the recovery window on a policy, and it applies to every artifact in that policy.

claims.claim: Full SharePoint site and OneDrive account restores have recovery points every 10 minutes for the prior two weeks.
claims.quote: For full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores, recovery points are available every 10 minutes for the prior two weeks, and weekly beyond two weeks through the configured recovery window of up to 10 years.

claims.claim: Full SharePoint and OneDrive restores use weekly recovery points beyond two weeks through the configured window.
claims.quote: For full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores, recovery points are available every 10 minutes for the prior two weeks, and weekly beyond two weeks through the configured recovery window of up to 10 years.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Granular file and folder restore remains limited to the most recent 14 days regardless of the configured window.
claims.quote: Granular file and folder restore is available only for recovery points within the most recent 14 days. ... Configuring a longer recovery window doesn't extend granular restore availability.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Recovery points older than 14 days support full OneDrive account or SharePoint site restore only.
claims.quote: Recovery points older than 14 days support full OneDrive account or SharePoint site restores only.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Increasing the window does not create older recovery points.
claims.quote: Increasing the recovery window doesn't create older recovery points or recover points that have already expired.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Increasing the window does not recover expired recovery points.
claims.quote: Increasing the recovery window doesn't create older recovery points or recover points that have already expired.

claims.claim: Available recovery history depends on when protection began and on recovery points not having expired.
claims.quote: Only recovery points that have been generated and haven't expired are available. ... Megan can't restore to a point before protection began or to a recovery point that has already expired.

claims.claim: What's new dates configurable recovery windows from 3 months to 2 years to September 18, 2026.
claims.quote:
Configure backup recovery windows

September 18, 2026

Backup policies can use recovery windows of 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years.

claims.claim: What's new dates the SharePoint and OneDrive extension to 10 years to October 31, 2026.
claims.quote:
Extend SharePoint and OneDrive recovery windows up to 10 years

October 31, 2026

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Deleted content remains in backup until the configured recovery window lapses, so a longer window retains it longer.
claims.quote: Deleted or versioned content held in the recycle bin or in the mailboxes will expire from the backups once the configured backup recovery window lapses

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: cost

claims.claim: Purview retention and deletion policies do not affect the backup recovery window.
claims.quote: Retention and deletion policies (for example, from Purview) don't affect the backup recovery window, which remains fully isolated from those policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft calls decreasing a recovery window a destructive action because older recovery points are deleted.

claims.claim: Decreasing a policy's window starts a 30-day grace period before recovery points older than the new window are deleted.
claims.quote: Decreasing a policy's window, or moving an item into a policy with a shorter window, starts a 30-day grace period before recovery points older than the new window are deleted.

claims.claim: Moving an item to a policy with a shorter window starts the same 30-day grace period before older points are deleted.
claims.quote: Decreasing a policy's window, or moving an item into a policy with a shorter window, starts a 30-day grace period before recovery points older than the new window are deleted.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup uses pay-as-you-go consumption billing, matching the consumption licensing model and variable cost rating.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Backup service, offered through the Microsoft 365 admin center, is a pay-as-you-go consumption-based service.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The pricing page lists $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.
claims.quote: The list price is $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.

claims.claim: The overview instead labels the OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange price as $0.15 per GB per month.
claims.quote: | Billing model | $0.15 per GB per month for all data protected by BackupRestores are free | $0.15 per GB per month for all data protected by BackupRestores are free | $0.15 per GB per month for all data protected by BackupRestores are free |

claims.claim: The overview states that restores are free.
claims.quote: $0.15 per GB per month for all data protected by BackupRestores are free

claims.claim: The billing calculation includes the live size of protected content.
claims.quote: Summation of the user-facing size of the protected content: ... Size of OneDrive accounts and SharePoint sites as displayed in the live sites' usage reports, which includes the first-stage recycle bin.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; summary; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing calculation also includes deleted and versioned data held for recovery.
claims.quote: Summation of the deleted and versioned data held for recovery in the backups: ... Deleted content in SharePoint sites' and OneDrive accounts' second-stage recycle bin ... Deleted and versioned items in the protected mailboxes.

claims.claim: Expired deleted or versioned content stops contributing to billing when the configured recovery window lapses.
claims.quote: Once deleted or versioned content expires from the backups, they're no longer counted in the backup consumption equation and therefore no longer contribute to the cost.

claims.claim: The pricing page's example keeps deleted content billable for a year under a one-year recovery window.
claims.quote: If you delete content in that site such that it's now only 0.5 GiB, your next monthly bill will still be for 1 GiB since the backup tool is retaining that deleted content for a year.

claims.claim: Restore point frequency does not materially change backup storage cost.
claims.quote: The restore point frequency doesn't materially impact the cost of the backup storage, so reducing that frequency wouldn't change your costs.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft documents its Backup pricing calculator as a tool to estimate storage and cost.

claims.claim: The pricing calculator is an Excel spreadsheet linked from the pricing page.
claims.quote: Download the latest version of the Microsoft 365 Backup pricing calculator tool (an Excel spreadsheet).

claims.claim: Estimating SharePoint and OneDrive backup storage includes live data and second-stage recycle bin sizes.
claims.quote: The Total Storage (GB) input field should include the sum of sizes of live data and sizes of recycle bins and mailbox online archives in your tenant.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup pay-as-you-go billing is linked to an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: As a first step, you should link an Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go, if you haven't already done so.

claims.claim: The pricing page does not state a separate price for longer recovery windows.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup long term recovery window 10 years pricing separate price example. Read backup-pricing, backup-overview and backup-whats-new; pricing states $0.15/GiB/month and expiration at the configured window, not a separate longer-window price.

claims.claim: The pricing page does not give a worked example for recovery windows beyond one year.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup long term recovery window 10 years pricing separate price example. Read the complete backup-pricing page: its recovery-window example uses one year; other examples concern aggregate storage or Entra objects, not multi-year windows.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Entra Premium recovery window is not configurable.

claims.claim: The SharePoint policy recovery-window control is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center via Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > policy > View details > Recovery window.

claims.quote: This method updates retention settings ... PATCH /solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies/{sharePointProtectionPolicyId}

claims.claim: The SharePoint update request sets retentionSettings in the request body.
claims.quote: retentionSettings ... Updated retention settings for the policy. If retentionSettings is omitted, the existing retention settings are unchanged. You can update retentionSettings without adding or removing protection units.

claims.claim: P3650D is a supported retentionSetting period for create and update requests.
claims.quote: The supported policy retention periods in create and update requests are: P90D, P180D, P365D, P730D, P1095D, P1460D, P1825D, P2190D, P2555D, P2920D, P3285D, and P3650D.

claims.claim: The retentionSetting interval R/P1W is used when specifying the policy retention period in a create or update request.
claims.quote: Use R/P1W when specifying the policy retention period in a create or update request.

claims.claim: The Graph API shown is beta, subject to change and not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Backup activity is viewed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Reports > Recent activities > View more.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup Activity Logs provide an in-product view ... Open Reports > Recent activities > View more to review activity counts and details, filter or search activities, and export the current results as a CSV file.

claims.claim: Administrators can export the current Backup activity results as a CSV file.
claims.quote: Open Reports > Recent activities > View more to review activity counts and details, filter or search activities, and export the current results as a CSV file.

claims.claim: Activity logs are retained for a fixed 365 days.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide recovery-window default control is documented; each SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange policy carries its own value.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup recovery window tenant-wide default retention settings policy. Read backup-view-edit-policies, backup-whats-new, backup-setup and the SharePoint update/retentionSetting references; results document per-policy values, not a tenant-wide default control.
